name: Printout proforma definition
purpose: The ppc table lists the monitoring parameters printed in each telemetry printout proforma declared in ppf: one record per parameter in the printout, with its position and the number format used to print its value (binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal or the normal engineering/raw form). The number of records per printout must equal PPF_NBPR. As for ppf, the ICD says these files need not be imported into the run-time database and can serve as initialisation files read directly by the printing application, and that printout proforma can currently be defined only with the SCOS-2000 editor. Importing them as specified would need extensions to the underlying data structures, so the table mainly documents the intended structure of a printout definition.

fields.name: PPC_NUMBE
fields.description: Name of the printout proforma; must match PPF_NUMBE of the corresponding printout. Part of the key.

fields.name: PPC_POS
fields.description: Position of the parameter in the printout. Part of the key.

fields.name: PPC_NAME
fields.description: Name of the monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) printed in the printout.

fields.name: PPC_FORM
fields.description: Format used to print the parameter values. B, O and H apply only to raw values of unsigned integer parameters; N prints the engineering value for calibrated parameters, otherwise raw decimal.

values.meaning: Binary; only applicable to raw values of unsigned integer parameters
Octal; only applicable to raw values of unsigned integer parameters
Hexadecimal; only applicable to raw values of unsigned integer parameters
Normal: the engineering value is shown for parameters associated with one or more calibration definitions, otherwise the raw value in decimal

history: Unchanged in field names, types and keys from ICD 5.1 §3.3.2.6.8 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.58) through ICD 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.117-118), ICD 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.121-122) and ICD 7.0 §3.3.2.7.8 (PDF p.124-125). The only wording change is that the 'N' format refers to 'one or more calibration definitions' instead of 'a calibration curve', following the ICD 6.0 introduction of multiple calibrations per parameter. Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).
notes: ppc.dat is empty (0 bytes) in both Solar Orbiter releases and in the SWA IDB; the database has only a placeholder COL1. pyscos2000 has no ppc model. The HPSDB note (h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb, PDF p.31) requires ppc to be absent.
